question: What is a load balancer and what problem does it solve?
answer_hinglish:
Load balancer ek component hai jo aane wali requests ko kai servers (upstreams) mein baant deta hai. Problem yeh hai ki ek server ki capacity limited hoti hai: CPU, memory, connections. Agar saari traffic ek hi server par jaye toh woh slow ya down ho jata hai, aur woh single point of failure bhi ban jata hai. Load balancer se hum horizontal scaling kar sakte hain: zyada traffic ke liye zyada servers jodo, client ko wahi ek address dikhta rahe.

Is project mein `Balancer` class (src/balancer.ts) yeh kaam karti hai: `UPSTREAM=http://a:3000,http://b:3000` do upstreams deta hai, aur har request ke liye `acquire()` ek target chunta hai. Do strategies hain: round-robin aur least-connections.

Dhyan rakho: abhi (stage 2) mein health checks nahi hain, toh load balancer sirf baant'ta hai; woh yeh nahi jaanta ki koi upstream mar chuka hai. Isliye abhi yeh poora failover nahi hai. Wo stage 3 mein aayega. Interview mein yeh farak saaf bolna: balancing aur availability alag cheezein hain.
why_needed: Ek server ki limit se aage scale karna aur ek server ke fail hone par poora system na girne dena.
real_world_analogy: Bank ke counters: ek counter par line lambi ho toh doosre counter khol dete hain, aur ek guard line ko baant'ta hai.
how_it_works: Request aati hai, balancer ek upstream chunta hai, proxy usko forward karta hai, aur response wapas client ko jata hai. Client ko pata nahi chalta ki kaunsa server mila.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::Balancer.acquire() target chunta hai; proxy.ts::createProxy handle() mein lease leta hai aur target ke host/port par http.request banata hai.
advantages: Ek server band hone par baaki chalte rahenge (health checks ke saath)
disadvantages: Balancer khud ek component hai jise HA chahiye
Stateful apps ke liye sticky sessions jaise extra decisions
common_mistakes: Load balancing aur failover ko ek hi cheez samajhna
Balancer ko single instance chhod dena

question: How does round-robin work, and when does it distribute badly?
answer_hinglish:
Round-robin simple hai: upstreams ki list mein ek counter chalta hai, aur har nayi request agle upstream ko jati hai: A, B, C, A, B, C. Is project mein `pickRoundRobin()` mein `this.next` index rakhta hai aur modulo karke agla target deta hai. Yeh load ko ignore karta hai: woh yeh nahi dekhta ki A abhi kitni requests par atka hai.

Jab sab requests lagbhag barabar kaam ki hoti hain aur sab servers barabar tez hain, toh round-robin bilkul theek aur sabse sasta hai: koi state nahi, koi measurement nahi. Problem tab aati hai jab requests ka cost alag alag ho. Misal: koi request 5 ms ki, koi 30 second ki report. Agar ek server par kuch lambi requests ek saath aa jayein, toh round-robin phir bhi usko har N-vi request deta rahega, aur uski queue badhti jayegi.

Is project ka test `ignores load: a busy target still gets its turn` yeh behaviour pakadta hai. Isliye uneven requests ke liye least-connections ka option hai.
why_needed: Sabse simple strategy samajhna, aur uski limitation jaanna.
real_world_analogy: Teacher har bachche ko baari baari se sawaal puchti hai, chahe kisi ne pichla jawab dene mein 10 minute laga diye hon.
how_it_works: Ek integer index, har pick par index+1 modulo n. Koi load measurement nahi.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::pickRoundRobin; tests: cycles through the targets in order, ignores load: a busy target still gets its turn; integration: spreads 9 sequential requests evenly, in order.
disadvantages: Request ka cost ya server ki speed nahi dekhta
Ek slow server par bhi barabar traffic
common_mistakes: Sochna ki round-robin hamesha 'fair' hai
Alag capacity wale servers par weights ke bina use karna
follow_up_questions: Weighted round-robin kaise karoge?
Round-robin ek restart ke baad kahan se shuru hota hai?

question: How does least-connections work, and why is it better than round-robin for uneven requests?
answer_hinglish:
Least-connections har upstream ki active requests ginta hai (jo abhi chal rahi hain, finish nahi hui) aur nayi request us upstream ko deta hai jiske paas sabse kam hain. Idea simple hai: jo server atka hai uski active count badhti rehti hai, toh usko kam nayi requests milti hain. Jo server jaldi kaam khatam karta hai, uski count jaldi gir jati hai aur usko zyada milti hain. Yeh apne aap load ke hisaab se adjust hota hai bina server speed ko alag se measure kiye.

Is project mein `Target.active` har upstream ka counter hai. `acquire()` pick karke `target.active++` karta hai; request khatam hone par `lease.release()` ise `--` karta hai.

Test `steers new requests away from an upstream that is stuck on a slow request` yeh asli HTTP servers par dikhata hai: ek upstream pehli request ko hold karke baitha hai, aur baad ki 6 requests sab doosre upstream ko jati hain. Phir slow response chhodne par counter wapas 0 ho jata hai. Round-robin yahi 6 requests aadhi aadhi baant'ta, aur 3 us atke server par chali jaatin.

Limitation: yeh requests ki ginti ginta hai, unka bhaar nahi. Ek 10 GB upload aur ek chhoti GET dono 1 connection hain.
why_needed: Uneven requests (uploads, reports) wale workloads mein load sahi baantna.
real_world_analogy: Supermarket ki line mein sabse chhoti line chunna: jahan cashier atka hai wahan line lambi dikhti hai.
how_it_works: Har request par O(n) scan: sabse kam active wala target chuno, uska active++ karo; release par active--.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::pickLeastConnections aur Target.active; proxy.ts res 'close' par lease.release().
advantages: Load ke hisaab se apne aap adjust hota hai
Slow ya stuck upstream se traffic hat jata hai
disadvantages: O(n) scan har request par
Requests ginta hai, unka weight nahi
Counter per process hai (agle sawaal dekho)
common_mistakes: Counter ko release karna bhool jana (leak)
Sochna ki yeh health check ka replacement hai
follow_up_questions: Least-connections kab round-robin se kharab ho sakta hai?
Weighted least-connections kaise banaoge?

question: Why does least-connections rotate through ties instead of always choosing the first target?
answer_hinglish:
Maan lo teen upstreams hain aur teeno idle hain, matlab teeno ki active count 0 hai. Agar code hamesha 'pehla jo minimum ho' chune, toh har request pehle upstream ko jayegi jab tak woh ek ya zyada requests par busy na ho jaye. Chhote ya sequential traffic mein (jaise ek ke baad ek requests, har ek turant finish) pehla server hi saara kaam karega, aur baaki idle rahenge. Load balancer ka matlab hi khatam.

Isliye `pickLeastConnections()` scan ko wahan se shuru karta hai jahan pichla pick khatam hua tha (`this.next`) aur sirf STRICTLY chhoti count milne par best badalta hai (`<`, `<=` nahi). Nateeja: jab sab barabar hon, toh scan ka starting point har baar aage badhta hai aur tie rotate hoti hai: A, B, C, A, B, C.

Test `rotates among ties instead of always choosing the first target` har pick ke baad lease release karta hai (sab idle) aur dekhta hai ki picks a,b,c,a,b,c aate hain. Maine `<` ko `<=` karke dekha: tab yeh test (aur kuch aur) fail hote hain, yaani tie rule sach mein tested hai.
why_needed: Idle ya lightly loaded system mein bhi traffic sahi baantna.
real_world_analogy: Teen khali counters ke saamne guard hamesha pehle counter par bhejta rahe toh baaki do bekaar hain.
how_it_works: Scan offset (next) se shuru, strict '<' se compare. Pick ke baad next = chuna hua index + 1.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::pickLeastConnections; test: rotates among ties instead of always choosing the first target.
advantages: Idle pool mein bhi traffic barabar
disadvantages: Random choice se zyada predictable lekin tie-breaking synchronized ho sakta hai agar kai proxies ek saath chalein
common_mistakes: `<=` use karna
Hamesha index 0 se scan karna
follow_up_questions: Random tie-breaking ke kya fayde hain?

question: What is the lease pattern used by Balancer, and why is release idempotent?
answer_hinglish:
`acquire()` sirf target nahi deta, ek `Lease` object deta hai jisme `target` aur `release()` hai. Lease ka matlab: 'maine is upstream par ek slot liya hai, aur kaam khatam hone par wapas dunga'. Jab tak release nahi hota, `target.active` mein woh request gini jati hai.

Release idempotent hai: andar ek `released` flag hai, aur pehli call ke baad dobara call koi asar nahi karti. Yeh isliye zaroori hai ki Node mein ek request ke khatam hone ke kai raaste ho sakte hain (response finish, error, client abort), aur kabhi kabhi do events ek hi request ke liye fire ho sakte hain. Agar release non-idempotent hota, toh ek double call counter ko negative bana deta, aur least-connections us upstream ko 'bahut khali' samajh ke uspe sab bhej deta.

Is project mein release sirf ek jagah hota hai: `res.on("close")`. Test `release is idempotent: a double release does not undercount` aur `returns to zero after success, upstream failure, client abort and a mid-response drop` dono is design ko cover karte hain. Maine release ko comment karke dekha: do tests fail hue.
why_needed: Counter ko galat hone se bachana, kyunki least-connections poori tarah isi counter par tika hai.
real_world_analogy: Library ki kitaab: issue karte waqt entry, wapas karte waqt entry kategori; do baar wapas karne par bhi record sirf ek baar kate.
how_it_works: Closure ke andar `released` boolean. Pehli release par active--, baad ki calls return.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::acquire (Lease), proxy.ts: let lease; res.on('close') mein lease?.release().
advantages: Ek hi jagah release: leak dhoondhna aasan
disadvantages: Agar release kabhi call hi na ho toh leak (isliye close event par, jo har raaste mein fire hota hai)
common_mistakes: Har event handler mein alag release karna
Release ko success path tak seemit rakhna
follow_up_questions: Close event kya har case mein fire hota hai?
Lease ko timeout ke saath kaise banaoge?

question: Why does the balancer need no lock, and when would it need one?
answer_hinglish:
Node.js ka JavaScript code ek hi thread par chalta hai. `acquire()` poora synchronous hai: target chuno aur `active++` karo, beech mein koi await ya callback nahi. Isliye do requests ek saath `acquire()` ke andar interleave nahi ho sakti; ek khatam hogi, tab doosri shuru. Isse 'check phir update' wali race condition (jaise P01 ka naive GET/SET limiter) yahan possible nahi hai, aur lock ki zaroorat nahi.

Yeh tab badal jata hai jab: (1) hum worker threads ya cluster mein shared memory (SharedArrayBuffer) mein counters rakhein -- tab atomics ya lock chahiye; (2) pick aur increment ke beech koi `await` aa jaye (jaise health check ya async config lookup) -- tab doosri request beech mein ghus sakti hai aur dono ko ek hi target mil sakta hai.

Multiple processes ke case mein (cluster ya multiple systemd instances) har process ka apna counter hai, toh lock ki nahi, coordination ki baat hoti hai. Yeh design property hai, aur koi test iska 'proof' nahi deta; yeh Node ke execution model par depend karta hai. Comment `balancer.ts` mein bhi yehi likha hai.
why_needed: Concurrency ke correctness arguments ko aasan aur sahi rakhna.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi cashier ek hi register par: do log ek saath register nahi khol sakte.
how_it_works: Event loop ek baar mein ek callback chalata hai. Synchronous function ke andar koi doosra callback nahi chalta.
in_this_project: balancer.ts: acquire() mein pick aur target.active++ ek hi synchronous block mein hain; class ke upar comment bhi.
advantages: Simple code, lock ya atomics nahi
disadvantages: Yeh sahi tabhi tak jab tak beech mein await na aaye
Multi-process mein counters share nahi hote
common_mistakes: Pick aur increment ke beech await daalna
Samajhna ki Node mein concurrency ka koi issue hota hi nahi
follow_up_questions: Agar pick ke beech await aa jaye toh kya hoga?
Worker threads mein counters kaise share karoge?

question: With several proxy processes, least-connections counters are per process. What goes wrong and what are the options?
answer_hinglish:
Agar hum ek server par 4 proxy processes chalayein (CPU cores ke liye) toh har ek apna `Balancer` aur apna `active` counter rakhta hai. Process 1 ko lagta hai ki upstream A par 3 requests hain, jabki asal mein A par kul 12 hain (4 processes x 3). Har process sirf apna hissa dekhta hai. Result: least-connections 'locally optimal' hai lekin globally nahi; kisi upstream ko jyada load mil sakta hai jabki har process ko woh kam busy dikhe.

Options: (1) Sab kuch ek process mein (simple, ek core limit). (2) Processes ke aage L4 balancer jo connections ko evenly baante (isse har process ko lagbhag barabar traffic milta hai, aur local counters kaafi hote hain). (3) Shared counters (Redis ya shared memory): sahi hai lekin har request par ek network call, latency aur ek naya failure point. (4) Power-of-two-choices jaisi sampling jo local information par bhi theek chalti hai.

Is project mein abhi option (1) hai: single process, aur README mein likha hai ki counters per process hain. Hum koi multi-process measurement nahi kar chuke, isliye kisi option ko 'better' number ke saath claim nahi karte.
why_needed: Scaling ke saath balancing ka correctness kaise badalta hai, yeh samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Ek restaurant mein do waiters: har ek sirf apne tables ki line dekhta hai, toh kitchen ko dono ka total load dikhta hi nahi.
how_it_works: Counters process memory mein hain. Processes ke beech koi shared state nahi, isliye har ek apne view se decision leta hai.
in_this_project: balancer.ts: Balancer instance per createProxy call; README mein 'per process' note.
advantages: Local counters sasti aur tez hain
Zyadatar workloads mein approximate load balancing kaafi hoti hai
disadvantages: Global view nahi
Zyada processes par error badh sakta hai
common_mistakes: Process-local counters ko global maan lena
Shared Redis counters ko bina soche hot path par daalna
follow_up_questions: Redis ke shared counters ki latency ka asar kya hoga?
Power of two choices kyun kaam karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Local counters = tez, simple, approximate. Shared counters = accurate, par har request par network hop aur extra failure point. Kai systems approximate local view chunte hain kyunki balancing ko perfect hone ki zarurat nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek process restart: uske counters 0 se shuru, toh usko lagta hai sab idle hain aur woh ek burst kisi ek upstream par bhej sakta hai. Shared Redis down: ya toh fail-open local par ya requests fail.
advanced.alternatives: L4 load balancer processes ke aage; power-of-two-choices; consistent hashing (har client ek hi upstream par); shared counters.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par processes zyada hote hain aur local views aur noisy: ek L4 layer upar zaroori ho sakti hai. 100x par multiple servers ke proxies par DNS ya cloud balancer.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-upstream active gauge metrics har process se, L4 distribution, aur ek load test jo dikhaye ki local counters real mein kitna skew karte hain (abhi measure nahi kiya).

question: What happens today when one of the upstreams is dead? Is this high availability?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi (stage 2) mein koi health check nahi hai, isliye dead upstream bhi rotation mein rehta hai. Round-robin ke saath do upstreams (ek zinda, ek dead) mein har doosri request dead wale ko jati hai aur 502 deti hai. Test `still sends its share of traffic to a dead upstream (health checks come in stage 3)` exactly yeh dikhata hai: statuses [200, 502, 200, 502].

Toh yeh high availability nahi hai. Load balancing sirf requests baant'ta hai; availability ke liye yeh bhi chahiye ki marne wale server ko rotation se nikaala jaye (health checks) aur failed idempotent requests ko doosre upstream par retry kiya jaye. Dono stage 3 mein plan hain, aur abhi implemented nahi hain.

Least-connections ke saath thoda alag behaviour: dead upstream par connection turant refuse hoti hai, toh uski active count jaldi 0 ho jati hai, aur woh balancer ko 'sabse khali' dikhta hai, aur zyada requests usi ko milti hain. Yeh ek real known pitfall hai (fast-failing server traffic magnet ban jata hai). Maine isko alag test se nahi dekha, toh yeh reasoning hai, measured fact nahi.
why_needed: Honestly batana ki system kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi.
real_world_analogy: Bus mein ek bhi seat nahi hai par conductor sab ko usi bus mein bithata raha: baantna aur sahi jagah bhejna alag cheezein hain.
how_it_works: Balancer ko kisi upstream ki health ka koi signal nahi milta, sirf active counts. Connection error aane par proxy 502 deta hai lekin balancer ko yeh yaad nahi rehta.
in_this_project: balancer.ts mein health ka concept nahi; test loadbalancing.test.ts 'what stage 2 does NOT do'.
disadvantages: Real traffic par failures ka share seedha users tak jata hai
common_mistakes: Load balancing ko HA bolna
Fast-failing upstream ke traffic magnet banne ko ignore karna
follow_up_questions: Passive vs active health checks mein kya fark hai?
Fail-fast server least-connections ko kaise fool karta hai?

question: What if a request ends in a way the balancer never hears about (leak)? How is the lease designed and tested to prevent that?
answer_hinglish:
Least-connections ki saari correctness is counter par hai. Agar kisi raaste se release call hi na ho (jaise error path mein bhool gaye), toh us upstream ki `active` count kabhi gir ti hi nahi, aur dheere dheere woh 'hamesha busy' dikhne lagta hai. Sabse bura case: ek upstream ki count itni badh jaye ki usko traffic milna hi band ho jaye, jabki woh bilkul theek hai.

Is project mein release ek hi jagah hai: `res.on("close")`. Node ka `close` event response ke saath har tarah ke ant par aata hai: normal finish, client disconnect, ya hamara res.destroy(). Isliye jo bhi path ho, release chalta hai.

Test `returns to zero after success, upstream failure, client abort and a mid-response drop` chaar upstreams banata hai (ok, dead, hang, cut) aur dekhta hai ki sab ke baad counters [0,0,0,0] hain. Test yeh bhi check karta hai ki hang wali request ke dauran `active` sach mein 1 tha, taaki test khali na ho. Release ki line comment karne par yeh test aur ek aur test fail hue.

Aur ek limitation: agar `close` event kabhi na aaye (Node bug ya ek bahut hi ajeeb socket state) toh leak ho sakta hai; iske liye ek timeout-based lease expiry ya periodic reconcile ek improvement hoga, jo abhi nahi hai.
why_needed: Resource accounting bugs chup chaap system ko kharab karte hain; unko design aur tests se rokna.
real_world_analogy: Parking lot jahan exit gate ka counter nahi chalta: lot 'full' dikhta hai jabki khali hai.
how_it_works: Node ka http server 'close' event har response ke ant par fire karta hai. Hum usi par release lagate hain.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: res.on('close') mein lease?.release() aur log; test accounting.
disadvantages: Close event par poori nirbharta; koi backup reconcile nahi
common_mistakes: Alag alag handlers mein release
Test mein counter ko zero check karna lekin kabhi non-zero na dekhna
follow_up_questions: Counter ko reconcile karne ka periodic job kaise likhoge?
Kya close event kabhi fire na ho sakta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek release point simple aur reviewable hai, lekin us ek event par single dependency. Alternative: har path mein explicit release (zyada code, zyada bugs) ya timeout-based lease expiry (extra complexity).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Missed release -> upstream permanently 'busy'. Double release -> negative count, upstream magnet (idempotent flag se roka). Process restart -> counters zero, in-flight requests ka hisaab gaya.
advanced.alternatives: Lease with TTL; periodic reconcile jo asli open sockets se compare kare; metrics-driven alert agar active kabhi zero na ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par ek chhoti leak bhi jaldi dikhti hai: alert chahiye (active gauge jo idle par zero na ho).
advanced.production_improvements: Per-upstream active gauge export, alert on 'active > 0 jab traffic zero', lease expiry, aur soak test.

question: How do you choose between round-robin and least-connections for a real service?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle workload dekho. Agar sab requests lagbhag barabar kaam ki hain (chhoti JSON API calls, 5 to 20 ms) aur servers barabar hain, toh round-robin kaafi hai: simple, O(1), predictable. Agar requests ka cost bahut alag hai (kuch milliseconds, kuch seconds ya minutes: reports, uploads, long polling), toh least-connections behtar hai kyunki woh atke hue server se traffic hata deta hai.

Dusre factors: server ki capacity barabar nahi ho toh dono ko weights chahiye (abhi nahi hain). Agar upstream ka failure fast hota hai (turant error) toh least-connections ek fast-failing server ko magnet bana sakta hai, jab tak health checks na ho. Agar proxy ke multiple processes hain toh least-connections ka local view approximate hai.

Is project mein default round-robin hai, aur `STRATEGY=least-connections` se badal sakte hain. Stage 4 mein ek slow upstream (40 ms extra) ke saath measure kiya (PROXY-079): least-connections ne slow ko sirf 7.3 percent traffic diya (round-robin: 50 percent), req/s 1524 se 3400, median latency 15 se 6 ms. Lekin tail (p99) behtar nahi hua: 46 vs 49 ms.
why_needed: Algorithm ko workload se match karna, fashion se nahi.
real_world_analogy: Chhote barabar kaam ke liye baari baari se baantna theek; kaam ka size alag ho toh dekhna padta hai kaun busy hai.
how_it_works: Round-robin: koi state nahi. Least-connections: per-upstream counter aur O(n) scan.
in_this_project: index.ts STRATEGY env se choose karta hai; balancer.ts dono strategies; README mein comparison table.
advantages: Switch sirf ek env var se
disadvantages: Koi weighted ya adaptive strategy abhi nahi
Koi measured comparison abhi nahi

Numbers invent karna

question: Why is the Balancer a separate class with no HTTP code in it?
answer_hinglish:
Separation of concerns: Balancer ka kaam sirf 'agla target kaun' batana hai; proxy.ts ka kaam HTTP lifecycle hai. Agar dono mile hote toh balancing ke tests ke liye har baar real servers aur sockets chahiye hote, aur tests slow aur flaky ho jaate. Ab `balancer.test.ts` bina kisi socket ke millisecond mein chalta hai aur tie-breaking ya counter jaise edge cases ko directly check karta hai.

Doosra fayda: stage 3 mein health checks aur retries jodte waqt hum Balancer ko extend karenge (jaise unhealthy targets ko skip karna) bina proxy.ts ka request lifecycle chheede. Teesra: `createProxy` mein `balancer` option hai, toh tests balancer ka reference rakh ke counters ko bahar se dekh sakte hain; yeh dependency injection ka chhota example hai.

Trade-off: ek extra abstraction aur ek extra file; ek chhote project ke liye over-engineering lag sakta hai. Lekin yahan test-ability aur stage 3 ke liye extensibility dono ka faayda mila.
why_needed: Logic ko I/O se alag rakhna test aur badlav dono aasan banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Dispatcher aur driver alag: dispatcher ko road ka pata nahi hona chahiye, driver ko order ka.
how_it_works: Balancer pure data structure hai (targets, counters, strategy). proxy.ts usse acquire/release ke through baat karta hai.
in_this_project: balancer.ts (koi http import nahi), proxy.ts mein options.balancer injection, balancer.test.ts bina sockets ke.
disadvantages: Ek extra file aur API surface
common_mistakes: Balancer ke andar http.request call karna
Sirf integration tests likhna

question: Walk through Balancer.acquire() and pickLeastConnections() line by line.
answer_hinglish:
`acquire()`: pehle `this.strategy` dekhta hai aur `pickRoundRobin()` ya `pickLeastConnections()` se `target` chunta hai. Phir `target.active++`, ek `released` flag banata hai, aur `{ target, release }` return karta hai. `release` flag check karke ek hi baar `active--` karta hai.

`pickLeastConnections()`: `n` targets hain. `bestIndex` ko `this.next % n` se shuru karta hai (pichle pick ke baad ka position). Phir `step` 1 se n-1 tak chalta hai: `i = (this.next + step) % n` ek circle mein agla candidate hai. Agar `targets[i].active` bestIndex ke target se STRICTLY chhoti hai toh bestIndex = i. Loop ke baad `this.next = bestIndex + 1` taaki agli baar scan us se aage se shuru ho. Return `this.targets[bestIndex]`.

Dhyan do: `% n` zaroori hai kyunki `next` bada ho sakta hai (bestIndex + 1 == n ho sakta hai). `!` non-null assertion isliye hai ki `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` array element ko `T | undefined` banata hai, lekin hum jaante hain index valid hai. Complexity O(n) per pick, aur n chhota hota hai (upstreams ki sankhya).
why_needed: Interview mein code line by line explain karna aana chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Circle mein baithe logon mein sabse khali kursi wale ko dhoondhna, jahan se pichli baar ruke the wahin se.
how_it_works: Circular scan with strict minimum; state: next index aur per-target active.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::Balancer.acquire, pickLeastConnections.
disadvantages: O(n) scan
common_mistakes: Modulo bhoolna
Non-strict compare

Agar targets ki list runtime mein badle toh next index ka kya hoga?

question: Operators say one backend gets almost all the traffic. How do you investigate?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla kadam: data dekho, andaza mat lagao. Is project mein har log line mein `upstream` field hai (`host:port`), toh logs se count nikal sakte hain: kis upstream ko kitni requests gayi. Misal: `jq -r .upstream proxy.log | sort | uniq -c`.

Agle sawaal: kaunsi strategy chal rahi hai? Startup log mein `strategy` field hai. Round-robin mein agar ek hi upstream ko bahut zyada jaa raha hai toh ya toh upstream list mein duplicate entries hain, ya clients ek hi connection reuse kar rahe hain jahan keep-alive ki wajah se proxy se connection nahi, kuch aur layer (jaise upar ka L4 balancer ya Caddy) imbalance kar rahi hai. Least-connections mein: ho sakta hai baaki upstreams ki requests lambi chal rahi hain toh unhe kam mil rahi hain (yeh expected hai), ya ek upstream fail-fast hai aur 502 de raha hai (count jaldi 0, toh zyada requests usi ko, `status` field dekho).

Check karo ki upstream URLs ek jaise hain (typo, alag ports) aur kya ek hi server ke do naam toh nahi. Maine ek 'distribution' tool nahi banaya hai; log analysis hi abhi ka tareeka hai.
why_needed: Production imbalance ko data se samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter par bhid ho toh pehle dekho kaun kaun kis counter par gaya (register), phir kaaran dhoondho.
how_it_works: Har request ek JSON line likhti hai: method, url, status, aborted, ms, upstream.
in_this_project: proxy.ts RequestLog.upstream; index.ts startup log mein strategy.
code_example:
jq -r '.upstream // empty' proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
jq -c 'select(.upstream=="10.0.0.2:3000" and .status>=500)' proxy.log | head
disadvantages: Koi metrics endpoint ya per-upstream gauge abhi nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sirf strategy ko doshi maan lena
Upstream URL typos check na karna
follow_up_questions: Per-upstream metrics kaise export karoge?
Fast-failing upstream ko log se kaise pehchanoge?

question: What does a pick cost, and how would you keep it cheap with hundreds of upstreams?
answer_hinglish:
Round-robin pick O(1) hai: ek index aur modulo. Least-connections O(n): har pick par saare targets scan hote hain. Hamare use case mein n chhota hai (2 se 10 upstreams), aur ek scan sirf n comparisons hai, jo HTTP parsing aur network I/O ke saamne bahut chhota hai. Isliye abhi koi optimisation nahi ki; maine isko measure bhi nahi kiya, toh 'negligible' ek reasoned estimate hai, measurement nahi.

Agar n sau ya hazaar ho jaye toh O(n) scan har request par noticeable ho sakta hai. Options: (1) min-heap ya bucket structure jo sabse kam active wale ko O(log n) mein deta hai, lekin har release/acquire par heap update. (2) Power of two choices: do random targets chuno aur kam wala lo: O(1) aur load balancing quality kaafi acchi. (3) Upstreams ko groups mein baant ke do-level balancing.

Interview mein: pehle bolo ki measure karo, phir optimise. Premature optimisation yahan galat hoga kyunki n chhota hai, aur simple code ko correct rakhna zyada kimti hai.
why_needed: Complexity ka andaza lagana aur sahi samay par optimise karna.
real_world_analogy: 10 counters mein sabse chhoti line dhoondhna aasan; 1000 counters mein har baar sab dekhna nahi chalega.
how_it_works: Linear scan O(n); heap O(log n) with updates; power-of-two O(1) with sampling.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::pickLeastConnections ka loop.
advantages: Simple linear scan chhote n par kaafi
disadvantages: n bada hone par O(n) problem; abhi measure nahi kiya
common_mistakes: Bina measure kiye optimise karna
Sochna ki O(n) hamesha kharab hai
follow_up_questions: Power of two choices ki guarantee kya hai?
Heap ke saath release kaise handle karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Heap complexity aur bugs badhata hai; power-of-two choices approximate hai lekin O(1) aur practice mein kaafi accha. Chhote n par linear scan sabse simple aur sabse kam bug wala.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Heap aur counters ka mismatch (release par update bhoolna) subtle skew deta hai; sampling mein bad luck se kabhi suboptimal pick.
advanced.alternatives: Power of two choices, heap, bucketed counters, consistent hashing.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x upstreams par scan 10x slow par phir bhi chhota; 100x par sampling ya two-level balancing.
advanced.production_improvements: Pehle ek benchmark likho jo pick latency measure kare (abhi nahi hai), phir decide karo.

question: How do you add or remove an upstream today, and what happens to in-flight requests?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi upstream list startup par env var `UPSTREAM` se aati hai aur runtime mein badal nahi sakti. Toh ek upstream add ya remove karne ka tareeka: env badlo aur proxy process restart karo. Restart mein SIGTERM par graceful shutdown chalta hai (naye connections band, chalte requests poore hone dena, 10 second par force exit), isliye zyada tar in-flight requests complete ho jaati hain. Yeh flow ab test aur measure ho chuka hai (PROXY-087), aur ek defect fix hua.

Restart ke dauran proxy ek chhote waqt ke liye connections accept nahi karega. Production mein yeh gap Caddy ke upar wale layer par aise handle ho sakta hai: do proxy instances aur rolling restart. Abhi hamare paas ek hi instance hai, toh brief downtime possible hai.

Improvement: config reload (SIGHUP ya admin API) jo Balancer ka targets list atomically badle aur removed targets ko 'draining' mark kare: nayi requests nahi, lekin chalti requests khatam hone dein. Yeh stage 3 ya baad ke liye hai, aur abhi implemented nahi hai.
why_needed: Deploy aur scale operations ke effects ko pehle se jaanna.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein ek counter band karna: naye customer ko doosre counter par bhejo, jo andar hai usko khatam karne do.
how_it_works: Targets array constructor mein ban jati hai. Badalne ke liye naya Balancer chahiye, isliye restart.
in_this_project: index.ts: UPSTREAM parse at startup; shutdown() graceful; balancer.ts constructor targets.
code_example:
# change the list, then restart the service
UPSTREAM=http://10.0.0.1:3000,http://10.0.0.2:3000,http://10.0.0.3:3000
sudo systemctl restart reverse-proxy
advantages: Graceful shutdown in-flight ko bachata hai (untested)
disadvantages: Runtime reload nahi
Single instance par brief downtime
Draining nahi hai: restart par in-flight POST toot sakti hai
common_mistakes: Restart ko 'zero downtime' bolna
Draining ke bina upstream hata dena
follow_up_questions: Draining state ko Balancer mein kaise model karoge?
Zero-downtime restart ke liye kya chahiye?

question: Why must the upstream list come from configuration and never from the request?
answer_hinglish:
Agar proxy request ke kisi hissa (header, query ya path) se tay kare ki kis host par forward karna hai, toh attacker use apni marzi ke address par bhej sakta hai: internal services (127.0.0.1:6379 Redis), cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), ya private network ke admin panel. Yeh SSRF (server-side request forgery) kehlata hai, aur proxy ek bahut accha tool ban jata hai attacker ke liye kyunki woh trusted network ke andar baitha hai.

Is project mein upstream list sirf `createProxy` ke options se aati hai, jo startup par env var `UPSTREAM` se bani hoti hai. Request ka path (`req.url`) sirf path ke roop mein forward hota hai, host kabhi nahi chunta. `Host` header preserve hota hai lekin sirf upstream ko jaata hai, destination tay karne mein use nahi hota.

Constructor har URL ko validate karta hai (sirf http, koi path nahi). Yeh sab ek hi idea ke tahat hai: destination operator ka faisla hai, client ka nahi. Agar kabhi dynamic routing chahiye (jaise Host ke hisaab se), toh ek allowlist ke through hi karna chahiye.
why_needed: Proxy ko attacker ke haath mein internal network ka darwaza banne se rokna.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko address sirf dispatcher batata hai, receiver ke parcel par likha address blindly nahi maanta.
how_it_works: Destination static config se; request ka sirf path+query forward hota hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: validation loop in createProxy; target sirf lease.target.url se aata hai; index.ts env parse.
code_example:
const target = lease.target.url;        // from config, never from the request
http.request({ hostname: target.hostname, port: target.port || 80, path: req.url, /* ... */ });
advantages: Config review mein sab dikh jata hai
disadvantages: Dynamic routing ke liye alag allowlist design chahiye
common_mistakes: Host header se upstream chunna
Redirect (Location) ko follow karna
follow_up_questions: Host-based routing ko safely kaise karoge?
Cloud metadata endpoint ko kaise block karoge?

question: A proxy has no database today. Where would balancer state (health, counters, config) live if it needed to be shared?
answer_hinglish:
Honest jawab: is project mein koi database nahi hai. Balancer ka saara state process memory mein hai: targets, active counters, next index. Yeh bilkul theek hai jab ek hi proxy process ho: state chhota hai, restart par zero se shuru, aur kuch durable chahiye nahi.

Agar kabhi shared state chahiye (multiple processes ya servers), toh teen alag tarah ka data hai aur har ek ka ghar alag: (1) Config (upstream list, weights): ek config file ya store, kam badalta hai, restart ya reload par padha jata hai. Durable store ya sirf file kaafi. (2) Health state (kaun zinda hai): thoda temporary, seconds mein badalta hai; har proxy khud check kar sakta hai (simple), ya shared store mein likha ja sakta hai taaki sab ek jaisa dekhein. (3) Active counters: bahut tez badalte hain (har request), toh Redis jaise store mein har request par update hot path mein network hop jodta hai; isliye aksar local approximate counters ko hi chuna jata hai.

Rule of thumb: jitna tez badalne wala data, utna local rakho; jitna kam badalne wala aur sab ko sync chahiye, utna shared store mein. Yeh abhi design discussion hai, kuch bhi implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Interview mein 'state kahan rakhoge' ka sahi framework dena.
real_world_analogy: Notice board par permanent rules (config), ghadi par abhi ka time (health), aur har table ka chalta bill (counters) alag jagah rakhte hain.
how_it_works: State ko change frequency aur sharing need ke hisaab se classify karna.
in_this_project: balancer.ts: Balancer ki fields sab in-memory hain. Shared store ka koi code nahi.
advantages: Local state: tez, simple, koi dependency nahi
disadvantages: Local state restart par kho jata hai
Process ke beech sync nahi
common_mistakes: Har cheez Redis mein daal dena
Hot path par network call
follow_up_questions: Shared config ko atomically kaise reload karoge?
Health state ko consistent kaise rakhoge?

question: Design the traffic path for 3 app servers behind this proxy, including what to do about sessions and a second proxy.
answer_hinglish:
Basic layout: client -> Caddy (TLS) -> proxy (round-robin ya least-connections) -> 3 app servers. Agar apps stateless hain (session Redis ya JWT mein), toh koi bhi server koi bhi request sambhal sakta hai, aur balancing seedhi hai. Agar sessions app ki memory mein hain, toh ek user ki saari requests ek hi server par jaani chahiye: sticky sessions. Hamare proxy mein sticky sessions nahi hain; options: cookie ya IP-hash se consistent selection, ya (behtar) sessions ko shared store mein le jana, taaki apps stateless ho jayein.

Proxy khud single point of failure hai. Do proxies chalane ke liye unke aage ek aur layer chahiye: DNS multiple A records, ya cloud L4 load balancer, ya VRRP-jaisi floating IP. Tab har proxy ke counters alag hote hain (per process), jo least-connections ko approximate banata hai.

Hamare Oracle setup mein plan hai: Caddy -> proxy on portfolio-a2 -> apps on portfolio-a1. Abhi yeh deploy nahi hua aur health checks bhi nahi hain, toh yeh design hai, claim nahi. Zaroori security: A1 ke app ports sirf A2 ke IP ke liye khulein.
why_needed: Component ko poore system ke context mein rakhna.
real_world_analogy: Mall: main gate (Caddy), floor guide (proxy), dukaanein (apps); agar guide ek hi hai toh woh bhi ek point of failure hai.
how_it_works: Stateless apps + load balancer = easy scaling. Stateful sessions ko sticky ya shared store se solve karte hain. HA ke liye har layer redundant honi chahiye.
in_this_project: Implemented: balancer.ts + proxy.ts. Not implemented: sticky sessions, multiple proxies, health checks, deployment (stage 4).
code_example:
internet -> Caddy :443 (TLS)
          -> proxy 127.0.0.1:8080  (UPSTREAM=http://10.0.0.5:3000,http://10.0.0.6:3000,http://10.0.0.7:3000)
          -> 3 app servers (ports open only to the proxy's IP)
advantages: Apps stateless ho toh scaling aasan
Layers alag alag scale ho sakti hain
disadvantages: Proxy aur Caddy dono extra failure points
Sticky sessions abhi nahi
common_mistakes: Sticky sessions ko default samajhna
App ports poori internet ko kholna
follow_up_questions: Consistent hashing sticky sessions se kaise alag hai?
Proxy ko HA kaise banaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sticky sessions simple hain lekin load uneven karte hain aur failover par session kho jata hai. Shared session store apps ko stateless banata hai par ek aur dependency lata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek app down: health checks ke bina 502s (abhi). Proxy down: poori site down jab tak doosra proxy na ho. Network partition A2 se A1: sab requests 502 ya 504.
advanced.alternatives: Caddy ya nginx ke built-in upstream balancing; cloud load balancer; service mesh.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: zyada app servers, health checks aur retries zaroori. 100x: multi-layer balancing, autoscaling, aur observability.
advanced.production_improvements: Stage 3 health checks aur retries, metrics, proxy ka HA pair, private network between servers, aur stage 4 ke baad measured numbers.

question: What is the power-of-two-choices technique, and would it fit this balancer?
answer_hinglish:
Power of two choices ka idea: har request ke liye saare targets scan karne ke bajaye do targets random chuno aur unmein se kam active wale ko do. Yeh surprisingly accha kaam karta hai: theory mein 'ek random chuno' se maximum load bahut kam hota hai (ek exponential improvement), aur 'sabse kam' chunne se kuch hi kharab. Cost O(1) hai, aur sirf do counters padhne padte hain.

Fit: hamare chhote n (2 se 10) par full scan hi kaafi hai, aur deterministic hai (tests aasan). Lekin power-of-two do jagah madad kar sakta hai: (1) bahut bade n par scan cost kam karne ke liye, (2) multiple processes mein jahan har process ka local view purana ho sakta hai: do random choices 'sabke ek hi least-loaded target par toot padne' (herd effect) se bachati hain. Jab sab proxies ek hi target ko 'sabse khali' dekhte hain toh sab ek saath usi par daud jaate hain; randomness yeh sync tod deti hai.

Cost: randomness se tests deterministic nahi rehte, toh seeded RNG ya injected random function chahiye. Abhi yeh implement nahi hai; yeh ek design extension hai jise stage 3 ke baad ek separate strategy (`p2c`) ke roop mein jod sakte hain.
why_needed: Chhoti si idea se bade scale par load balancing sudharna aur herd effect samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Do dukaanon ki line dekh ke chhoti wali chun lena, bajaye saare shehar ki dukaanein ginne ke.
how_it_works: Sample two, compare active, pick smaller. Randomness herd effect todta hai.
in_this_project: Implemented nahi hai. Closest code: balancer.ts::pickLeastConnections (full scan).
disadvantages: Non-deterministic, test karna thoda mushkil
Pure least-connections se thoda kam optimal
common_mistakes: Sochna ki power-of-two har haal mein least-connections se behtar hai
Seed ke bina flaky tests
follow_up_questions: Herd effect kya hota hai?
Random function ko test ke liye kaise inject karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Full scan = optimal local pick, deterministic. P2C = O(1), robust to stale info, thoda randomness. Chhote n par full scan, bade n ya multi-proxy mein P2C.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Do randomly chuni hui targets dono dead ho sakte hain (health checks ke bina) aur request fail.
advanced.alternatives: Heap-based least-connections, consistent hashing, weighted random.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: n bada hone par scan expensive; P2C constant rehta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Injected RNG, health-aware sampling, aur ek load test jo p2c vs least-connections ka skew measure kare (abhi nahi hai).

question: Write a unit test proving least-connections avoids a stuck target and keeps using the fast one.
answer_hinglish:
Test ka plan: do targets banao, 'slow' aur 'fast'. Ek `acquire()` karo jo slow ko jaye (sab idle hai toh pehla target) aur uska lease kabhi release mat karo: yeh 'stuck request' hai. Phir paanch baar `acquire()` karo, har baar turant release karo (fast request jaise), aur har pick ka naam note karo. Assert karo ki saare paanch 'fast' hain.

Kyun kaam karta hai: slow ki active count 1 par atki hai; fast ki 0 aur 0 hi rehti hai kyunki har lease turant release hoti hai. Strict `<` compare ki wajah se fast ko hamesha chuna jata hai (0 < 1).

Yeh test balancer.test.ts mein `keeps sending to the target that finishes fast and avoids the one that is stuck` naam se hai. Maine least-connections ka comparison hata ke dekha (load ignore): tab yeh test fail hua, toh yeh test sach mein is behaviour ko pakadta hai. Is test ka integration version real HTTP servers ke saath loadbalancing.test.ts mein hai.
why_needed: Ek design property ko ek chhote deterministic test se pakka karna.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter par cashier chai pe gaya hai: aap hamesha doosre counter par jaate ho.
how_it_works: Unit test bina sockets ke Balancer ko seedha chalata hai aur acquire/release se load simulate karta hai.
in_this_project: test/balancer.test.ts mein yeh test hai aur pass hota hai.
disadvantages: Real HTTP behaviour ko cover nahi karta (uske liye integration test)
common_mistakes: Slow lease ko release kar dena
Sirf happy path test karna
follow_up_questions: Is test ko round-robin ke saath chalaoge toh kya hoga?
Weighted version ka test kaisa hoga?

question: Add a 'draining' flag to Target so a target stops receiving new requests but finishes the ones it has. Sketch the change and the test.
answer_hinglish:
Idea: `Target` mein `draining: boolean` field. Dono pick functions draining targets ko skip karenge. Jab sab draining ho toh error ya fallback chahiye (kya karna hai yeh decision hai, abhi koi default nahi). Chalti requests ka lease release normal chalega, isliye `active` neeche aayegi, aur jab 0 ho jaye toh target safely hata sakte hain.

Round-robin mein skip karna: index se shuru karke circle mein pehla non-draining dhoondho. Least-connections mein candidates se draining ko nikaal do. Edge case: `this.next` ko update karte waqt dhyan rakhna.

Test: do targets, ek ko draining mark karo; paanch acquire karo aur assert karo ki sab doosre ko gaye; draining wale ka purana lease release karo aur dekho `active` 0 hota hai. Yeh sketch hai; yeh repo mein implement nahi hai, aur mera claim sirf design tak hai. Isi ko stage 3 ke health checks se jodna natural hai: 'unhealthy' bhi ek tarah ka skip flag hai, jo ek baar mein dono ko handle karega.
why_needed: Runtime operations (drain) ke liye balancer ko extend karne ki soch.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan band karne se pehle 'naye customer nahi' ka board lagao, andar wale ka kaam khatam hone do.
how_it_works: Skip flag + same lease accounting. Release logic nahi badalta.
in_this_project: Not implemented; extension point balancer.ts::Balancer pick functions aur Target.
advantages: Health checks ke saath reuse hoga
disadvantages: Sab draining ho toh behaviour tay karna padega
Round-robin index ka subtle handling
common_mistakes: Draining target ke lease ko turant release kar dena
Skip logic ko dono strategies mein alag likhna
follow_up_questions: Sab targets draining ho toh kya return karoge?
Draining kaun set karega: admin API ya signal?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Skip flag chhota change hai lekin acquire ka return type nullable ho sakta hai, jo proxy.ts mein 503 handling maangta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Sab targets draining: requests ko 503 dena ya purane targets par fallback.
advanced.alternatives: Naya Balancer instance banake atomically swap karna (immutable approach), draining sirf operations layer par.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada upstreams par rolling deploys frequent hote hain: draining zaroori ho jata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Admin endpoint ya SIGHUP reload, metrics, aur health checks ke saath integration.

question: After some hours, least-connections never sends traffic to one healthy upstream. What do you suspect and how do you prove it?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla shak: counter leak. Us upstream ki `active` ki value kisi path par release na hone ki wajah se upar atki hai (ya process restart ke baad bhi? nahi, restart par zero hota hai). Jo upstream 'hamesha busy' dikhta hai woh kabhi chuna nahi jata.

Prove kaise karein: abhi hamare paas koi metrics endpoint nahi hai, toh sabse seedha tareeka ek debug log ya ek chhota admin endpoint jo `balancer.targets.map(t => t.active)` print kare, jab traffic ruka ho. Agar idle par bhi kisi target ki active > 0 hai, toh leak confirm. Dusra tareeka: us upstream ke `ss -tn` se asli open connections gino; agar kam hain aur counter bada, toh counter galat hai.

Root cause dhoondho: release `res.on('close')` par hai, toh woh path jahan close fire nahi hota ya lease banne ke baad exception ho gayi? Is project ka test chaar paths ke liye counters ko zero check karta hai, toh known paths clean hain; naye code ya Node bug ka shak karna padega. Fix: leak ka path dhoondh ke test likho; defense mein lease TTL ya reconcile job. Honest note: yeh debug endpoint abhi hai nahi.
why_needed: Chup chaap accounting bugs ko pakadne ki practice.
real_world_analogy: Parking lot ka board 'full' dikhata hai par camera mein khali: board galat hai, pehle ginti verify karo.
how_it_works: Counter vs asli connections ki tulna se pata chalta hai ki counter drift hua hai.
in_this_project: balancer.ts Target.active; proxy.ts res close release; test accounting.
code_example:
# compare the counter with real established connections to the upstream
ss -tn state established '( dport = :3000 )' | wc -l
advantages: Counter aur asli state ki tulna se evidence
disadvantages: Abhi koi metrics ya debug endpoint nahi
Reconcile mechanism nahi
common_mistakes: Seedha upstream ko doshi maan lena
Idle par counter check na karna
follow_up_questions: Active gauge Prometheus mein kaise export karoge?
Lease TTL kaise implement karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Reconcile job ya TTL leaks ko self-heal karte hain par masking bugs ka risk bhi hai: pehle alert, phir auto-fix.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Leak: upstream starve. Negative counter: upstream magnet (idempotent release se roka).
advanced.alternatives: Per-upstream gauge + alert; periodic compare with socket count; lease expiry.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par leak jaldi dikhta hai; alerting zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Active gauge metric, alert 'active>0 at zero traffic', chaos test jo random aborts bheje aur counters zero check kare.
